items.title: Anthropic's AI Model Chained Exploits Across Chrome, Windows, Linux
items.summary: An unreleased Anthropic model chained four bugs into a one-click Chrome sandbox escape, plus working exploits for Safari, Windows, and Linux, reporting 62 flaws to Google overall. The Linux chain leaked a kernel address in 48 minutes and got root five minutes later (CVSS 9.8), needing only initial prompting. (4 minute read)

items.title: Genie 4: DeepMind's Real-Time World Model Gets Native Audio
items.summary: Genie 4 generates interactive worlds in real time with native audio tied to the action, using Gemini Omni to anchor appearance and a Gemini 3.8 Flash model for scene continuity. It's a research preview for trusted testers and the AI Ultra waitlist only, with no resolution, latency, or benchmark numbers disclosed. Testers can now steer weather, objects, and physics in a generated scene just by typing. (3 minute read)

items.title: Qwenputer: A RISC-V CPU Compiled Into Qwen3.5's Weights
items.summary: A compiler, not training, turns Qwen3.5-4B into a working 32-bit RISC-V CPU, using the model's Gated DeltaNet state as RAM. It passes the official riscv-tests, ran 18 million instructions error-free, and scores 97.5% on DeepMind's div_big versus the base model's 72.5%. Code and weights are on GitHub and Hugging Face, running at about 3,200 tokens per second on a single 24GB GPU. (4 minute read)

items.title: Stanford Professors Sue Anthropic Over Pirated Training Books
items.summary: Six Stanford professors, including Tobias Wolff, opted out of the $1.5 billion Bartz settlement and filed Cruz v. Anthropic, alleging their books were pulled from shadow libraries LibGen and PiLiMi to train Claude. They're seeking up to $150,000 per infringed work plus a training injunction, on top of over 70 pending AI-copyright suits. The case tests whether Bartz's roughly $3,000-per-work rate holds up against authors who opted out. (4 minute read)

items.title: 44 AI Agents Ran an Automated Hacking Campaign in Japan
items.summary: CyberStrikeAI split an attack lifecycle across 44 specialized agents — recon, exploitation, C2, persistence, exfiltration, and auto-generated reporting — to hit at least 19 organizations in Japan, Taiwan, and Hong Kong in October 2026. The tool even generated Japanese-language phishing pages automatically. Researchers found no confirmed link to two other AI-assisted Japan campaigns in the same report, suggesting several groups are independently automating full attack chains now. (4 minute read)

items.title: AI Agents Pass Only 11% of Real Professional Tax Tasks
items.summary: Dayjob: Tax graded agentic models on 50 real multi-file tax engagements, some with over 100 files, against a 95% expert rubric. Claude Sonnet 5.5 led at just 10.8% pass@1, with Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 close behind at 9.6% and 9.2%. In one case, one model caught a residence-deadline issue in 5 of 5 tries while another missed it every time — the gap is in judgment, not arithmetic. (4 minute read)

items.title: A Script Hides Fake Bioweapon Code to Jailbreak AI Deobfuscators
items.summary: An obfuscated ad-fraud script embeds function names like computeRicinLethalDosageForWaterSupply and a hidden 'SYSTEM OVERRIDE' prompt, seemingly to make AI tools refuse to deobfuscate it. Two models, 'Astra' and 'Daybreak Blue', refused citing bio-risk; GLM-5.3 complied anyway. The fingerprinting code itself is ordinary browser tracking, but the decoy strings show attackers now engineering content specifically to trip LLM safety filters. (4 minute read)

items.title: A Domain-Specific Tokenizer Cuts LLM Inference Cost 77%
items.summary: VocabX rebuilds a model's tokenizer vocabulary for a target domain without touching weights or training data, shrinking a Qwen3-4B grader's output vocabulary from about 152,000 to 65,000 entries. On a production Portuguese essay grader, that cut measured inference cost 77% while accuracy rose, not fell. It beat the best reference method on token reduction across all 15 tested domain-and-model combinations. (4 minute read)
